## Key terms

{{< glossary vector-addition resultant-vector scalar-multiplication magnitude pythagorean-theorem unit-vector normalization speed velocity opposite-vector >}}

## 3.1 Two moves at once: adding vectors

- A raft paddles across a river, and the river pushes it. The raft makes two
  moves in every frame.
- Draw the second arrow from the head of the first: **head to tail**.
- The arrow from the first tail to the last head is the **sum** (the
  **resultant**).
- Rule: add the x-parts, and add the y-parts:
  a + b = (a~x~ + b~x~, a~y~ + b~y~).
- The order does not matter: a + b = b + a.
- Reverse question: the move you need = the move you want − the move you
  have.

![Paddle (0, 3) + current (2, 0) = real move (2, 3).](images/vector-add.png){width=72%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
(2, 0) + (0, 3) is **not** 5. The sum of two vectors is a vector: (2, 3).
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Head to tail in GeoGebra"}
At geogebra.org/calculator, type `u = Vector((3, 1))`, `v = Vector((1, 2))`
and `w = Vector((3, 1), (4, 3))`. Then type `u + v`. Does it end where w
ends? Write the components of u + v.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Adding moves"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(2, 2)|5|(4, 3)"}
A raft paddles (0, 3). The current is (2, 0). The real move per frame?
:   (2, 3)

In one frame a character walks (3, 0), the wind pushes (−1, 0) and a jump lifts (0, 4). The total move?
:   (2, 4)

What is (1, 0, 2) + (0, 4, −1)?
:   (1, 4, 1)

The current is (2, 0). Which paddle vector gives the move (0, 3)?
:   (−2, 3)

What is (−3, 2) + (3, −2)?
:   (0, 0)
:::
:::

## 3.2 Faster, slower, backwards: scaling a vector

- To scale a vector by a number k, multiply **both** components by k:
  k v = (k v~x~, k v~y~).
- k > 1: a longer arrow (a dash power-up, × 2).
- 0 < k < 1: a shorter arrow (slow motion, × 0.5).
- k = −1: the same length, the opposite direction (a ball bounces back).
- After n frames, an object has moved n × v: the velocity scaled by n.

![v = (2, 1) scaled by 2, by 0.5 and by −1.](images/scaling.png){width=80%}

{{< sim file="sims/vector-lab.html" poster="sims/vector-lab.png" title="Vector Lab: scale, measure and normalize a vector" height="640" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Scale it in Vector Lab"}
In **Vector Lab**, drag the arrow to v = (2, 1). Set k to 3, then 0.5, then
−2. Write down k v each time. Which values of k reverse the arrow?
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Scaling"}
A character runs with v = (3, 1) per frame. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(6, 1)|(3, −1)|(−6, −2)"}
A dash power-up doubles the velocity. The new velocity?
:   (6, 2)

Slow motion halves the velocity. The new velocity?
:   (1.5, 0.5)

A wall throws the character straight back (× −1). The new velocity?
:   (−3, −1)

Which number k makes the arrow shorter, in the same direction?
:   k = 0.5

The game is paused. It scales every velocity by…
:   0
:::
:::

## 3.3 How far away is it? The magnitude

- A guard attacks when the player is at most 5 units away. The game needs
  the **length** of the vector from the guard to the player.
- The components and the arrow make a right-angled triangle.
- **Pythagorean theorem:** |v| = √(v~x~² + v~y~²).
- In 3D: |v| = √(v~x~² + v~y~² + v~z~²).
- (−3)² = 9, so (3, 4), (−3, 4) and (3, −4) all have the length 5.
- Faster in games: compare the squares. In range if v~x~² + v~y~² ≤ 5².

![(3, 4) is 5 units long: 3² + 4² = 25 = 5².](images/magnitude.png){width=56%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
|(3, 4)| is **not** 3 + 4 = 7. The arrow goes straight across the triangle:
5.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Measure an arrow on paper"}
On squared paper (1 cm = 1 unit), draw the vector (6, 8). Measure it with a
ruler. Then calculate √(6² + 8²). Why is the arrow shorter than 6 + 8?
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · How far?"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="7|25|−9"}
The magnitude of (3, −4).
:   5

The magnitude of (0, −9).
:   9

The magnitude of (−5, 12).
:   13

Guard G = (1, 1), player P = (4, 5). The guard attacks at 5 units or less. Does it attack?
:   yes, the distance is 5

A drone flies (2, 3, 6). How far?
:   7
:::
:::

## 3.4 Only the direction: unit vectors

- An arrow on the screen points to the goal. It always has the same size.
  The game needs only the **direction**.
- A **unit vector** has the length 1. It shows only a direction.
- **Normalize** = divide by the magnitude: v̂ = v ÷ |v|.
- Example: (6, 8) ÷ 10 = (0.6, 0.8).
- Easy ones: (1, 0) right, (0, 1) up, (0, −7) → (0, −1).
- The zero vector (0, 0) has no direction. It cannot be normalized.

![(6, 8) and its unit vector (0.6, 0.8) on the circle of radius 1.](images/unit-vector.png){width=64%}

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Normalize in Vector Lab"}
In **Vector Lab**, switch on **Show unit vector**. Drag the arrow to (6, 8),
(0, −5) and (5, 12). Write the magnitude and the unit vector each time.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · Unit vectors"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(0, 7)|10|(1, 1)"}
Normalize (6, 8).
:   (0.6, 0.8)

Normalize (0, −7).
:   (0, −1)

Scale the unit vector (0.6, 0.8) back to the length 10.
:   (6, 8)

What is the magnitude of every unit vector?
:   1

The player stands on the goal. Why can the game not normalize the vector to the goal?
:   it is the zero vector
:::
:::

## 3.5 Same speed in every direction: direction times speed

- A top-down game: right = (1, 0), up = (0, 1), right + up = (1, 1).
- |(1, 1)| = √2 ≈ 1.41, so the diagonal move is about 41 % faster: a bug.
- The fix: velocity = speed × unit direction: v = s × d̂.
- The **speed** is the magnitude of the velocity: a scalar.
- Homing missile: direction = target − missile, normalize, then × speed.

![Without normalizing, the diagonal reaches farther. With normalizing, all directions reach the same circle.](images/diagonal.png){width=88%}

{{< sim file="sims/fair-speed.html" poster="sims/fair-speed.png" title="Fair Speed: the diagonal bug" kind="game" height="640" >}}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Speed × (target − missile) without normalizing is far too fast: 5 × (6, 8) =
(30, 40), a speed of 50.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Fair Speed"}
In **Fair Speed**, race the right runner and the diagonal runner with
**Normalize: off**, then with **Normalize: on**. Write down the four
distances. Explain the difference in one sentence.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 5 · Fair speed"}
Use √2 ≈ 1.41 and 1 ÷ √2 ≈ 0.71. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(4, 4)|4|(6, 8)"}
The speed is 4. Input (1, 1) without the fix. About how fast does the player move?
:   about 5.6

The same input (1, 1), normalized. About which unit vector?
:   (0.71, 0.71)

A missile at (2, 1) flies to (8, 9) with the speed 5. Its velocity?
:   (3, 4)

A missile uses 5 × (6, 8) without normalizing. What is its speed?
:   50

The speed of the velocity (3, 4).
:   5
:::
:::

## Game challenge: Raft Rush {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

**Raft Rush** is a river game. The river is 8 units wide. The current pushes
the raft c = (3, 0) per frame. The player chooses one paddle vector before
the raft starts, with a magnitude of **at most 5**. In every frame the raft
moves by paddle + current. In round 1 the jetty is at (4, 0), the dock is
straight across at (4, 8), and the raft must arrive in 2 frames.

{{< sim file="sims/raft-rush.html" poster="sims/raft-rush.png" title="Raft Rush: paddle + current" kind="game" height="700" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 6 · Round 1"}
Raft Rush: current (3, 0), paddle at most 5, jetty (4, 0), dock (4, 8),
2 frames. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(0, 4)|(4, 8)|3"}
The player paddles (0, 4). The real move per frame?
:   (3, 4)

The real speed of that move.
:   5

With paddle (0, 4), where is the raft after 2 frames?
:   (10, 8)

Which real move per frame reaches the dock in 2 frames?
:   (0, 4) per frame
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 7 · Plan the crossing (harder)"}
Raft Rush: current (3, 0), paddle at most 5, jetty (4, 0), dock (4, 8),
2 frames. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(3, 4)|(−6, 4)|about 4.5"}
Which paddle vector takes the raft straight to the dock in 2 frames?
:   (−3, 4)

The magnitude of that paddle vector. Is it allowed?
:   5, allowed

The unit vector of the paddle (−3, 4).
:   (−0.6, 0.8)

A faster river has the current (4, 0). The paddle for (0, 4) is (−4, 4). Is it allowed?
:   no, about 5.7 is more than 5

A turbo doubles the paddle (−3, 4). The new real move with the current (3, 0)?
:   (−3, 8)
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- Add vectors component by component: head to tail.
- Scale a vector by k: both components × k; a negative k reverses it.
- The magnitude is the length: √(x² + y²) (+ z² in 3D).
- A unit vector has length 1: normalize = divide by the magnitude.
- Velocity = speed × unit direction: the same speed in every direction.
